Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a focused document titled `2026 Helio Start paid-pilot high-support case review`. Review all seven mature cases from the 2026 paid pilot that exceeded 90 support minutes, clearly distinguish external owner-permission or network-allowlist coordination from ordinary integration troubleshooting, state which causes were ruled out across all seven cases, and explain what the findings mean for admission correctness and operational follow-up. Keep it claims-safe and concise.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "2026 Helio Start paid-pilot high-support case review", "body": "Review date: 2028-01-01

Scope
All seven mature workspaces in the 2026 Helio Start paid pilot that exceeded 90 account-level support minutes were reviewed. This is a descriptive case review, not a causal test of acquisition, onboarding, or any proposed remedy.

Case classification
- Cases 1–5: supported external-authority coordination after admission. Each required an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action by the customer’s owner or another authorized person. This is distinct from ordinary integration troubleshooting: the limiting action was held outside Helio, even though the workspace had been admitted.
- Cases 6–7: ordinary integration troubleshooting within the supported admitted setup path. These cases involved product/integration guidance, not an external owner-permission or network-allowlist dependency.

Cross-case findings
- All seven were classified; five were external-authority action cases and two were ordinary integration cases.
- Across all seven, no case involved billing, unsupported admission, stale state, or conflicting state.
- In each of the five external-authority cases, external-authority status was current and verified yes at admission, and the governed route and lifecycle views agreed.

Meaning for admission correctness
The review supports the conclusion that the external-authority field meaning and the admission decisions were correct for these cases. The evidence points to a setup-sequence and coordination gap after admission, not to an eligibility-definition, state-meaning, routing, or fail-closed defect. It therefore does not support weakening admission rules or changing the eligibility field. It also does not establish that the observed pattern is universal or that any remedy will reduce support effort.

Operational follow-up
- Keep external-system authority separate from Helio administrator proof and connector authentication.
- Provide connector-specific, non-state-changing pre-setup guidance when an admitted workspace’s selected connector requires an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action and the external-authority state is current and verified yes.
- Keep missing, stale, conflicting, pending, no, or not-sure authority states on the existing fail-closed or assisted route.
- Keep ordinary integration troubleshooting in the supported setup path and report it separately from external-authority coordination.
- Track future cases by cause, first-contact support minutes, handoff/response timing, and resolution outcome; do not reset the account-level support clock or combine the two mechanisms.

Bottom line
Five of seven high-support cases were coordination with an external authority; two were ordinary integration troubleshooting. The review identifies a targeted operational follow-up while preserving admission correctness and the existing eligibility, routing, and state controls. It does not by itself justify a paid-acquisition, staffing, causal, scale, pipeline, or forecast claim."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_199_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The document clearly says that all seven paid-pilot workspaces exceeding 90 support minutes were reviewed, with five requiring a supported owner-level permission or network-allowlist action after admission and two requiring ordinary integration troubleshooting. Missing or contradictory counts or categories must fail.

The document states that the review found none of the seven cases involved billing, an unsupported admission, stale state, or conflicting state. Any assertion that one of these causes occurred must fail.

The document explains that in every one of the five authority-action cases, external-authority status was current and verified yes at admission; therefore the external-authority meaning and admission decisions remained correct. It identifies setup sequencing—not eligibility—as the gap and directs follow-up toward setup sequencing or coordination while preserving the decision not to change eligibility. Missing or contradictory meaning must fail.

The document treats the high-support case findings as descriptive and does not claim or imply that they prove causal acquisition performance, improved activation, reduced support demand or support-effort improvement, or scalability. {"results":[{"check_id":"riley_199_02","passed":true,"reason":"The document says “All seven mature workspaces…that exceeded 90 account-level support minutes were reviewed,” classifies five as requiring “an owner-level permission or network-allowlist action” after admission and two as “ordinary integration troubleshooting,” and states that “no case involved billing, unsupported admission, stale state, or conflicting state.” It further says all five authority cases had status “current and verified yes at admission,” concludes that field meaning and admission decisions were correct, identifies a “setup-sequence and coordination gap…not…eligibility,” preserves the eligibility rules, and explicitly frames the review as descriptive rather than causal while disclaiming support-effort, acquisition, and scale claims."}]}
